report:
Review submitted: **REWORK**.

Both of Root's preliminary suspicions checked out as confirmed defects:

1. **`prepare_reader638_release.py`** doesn't invoke any package producer — it only recomputes article/ref counts from two JSON files and returns a dict of hardcoded identity strings. It never calls the house's `verify_inputs`/`extract_immutable`/`archive_and_verify`, never checks a Web/review/checksum pin, and never creates an archive. `load_library()` is defined but dead — never called.

2. **`prepare_reader638_remote.py`** only string-replaces two `version==54/52` literals and the build id inside the inherited guard/script text. It has no `main()`, no `collection_script()`, and no `validate_package()` — so the collection/count consumers that actually bind the final receipt to 279/160/158 are never touched, and there's no real execution entry point at all.

All reported SHA-256 hashes matched the actual files, and the 3 tests genuinely pass — but they only exercise count-math/string-presence helpers, never the missing archive/collection/execution logic, so they can't substitute for the incomplete implementation. Full findings and a concrete remediation path (mirror `prepare_library_release.prepare()` / `prepare_library_remote.validate_package()`/`collection_script()`) are recorded in the review note on `task-670da6e315ad459286d7c7db84b4be41`.
